sentences.text: Revenue grew from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025, a 6.4% CAGR, with a cyclical trough in FY2020 when revenue fell 22.4% [F1][F10][F201][D198].
Operating margin rose from 3.0% to 16.5% over the window, and operating income compounded at 28.6% [F21][F30][F202].
The FY2020 fall reflected lower sales volume from weaker end-user demand and changes in dealer inventories [P59], and operating margin dropped 4.5pp [D211].
The FY2023 operating margin rose 6.0pp [D370] on favorable price realization and higher volume, with no repeat of the 2022 Rail goodwill charge [P31].
Power Energy, 47.6% of FY2025 revenue [D757], added 5.2pp to growth [D759], more than the 4.3% total [D463].
Total growth of 4.3% [D463] reflected higher sales volume from end-user equipment demand, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P13].
Construction Industries sales fell 1.6% [D765] on unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher volume [P8].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% [D467], less than the 17.7% drop in net income [D465], as diluted shares fell 3.5% [D483] and offset part of the decline.
Operating margin of 16.5% [F30] is above its 14.3% window median [D1123] but 3.7pp below the FY2024 high of 20.2% [D476][D1122].
Operating profit fell 14.7% [D464], mainly on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion that the filing ties to higher tariffs [P9].
In the FY2025 margin bridge, cost of revenue took 4.2pp off margin [D490], while R&D and SG&A were roughly neutral [D491][D492].
Incremental margin was -69.1% [D488], as operating costs grew 9.1% [D481] against revenue growth of 4.3% [D463].
Net margin of 13.1% [F50] trails operating margin by 3.4pp [F30], as the tax rate rose to 24.0% [D449] from 19.7% [D396]; the cited passages do not explain the tax move.
Free cash flow of $8.9 billion [F100] equalled 1.00x net income [D451], close to the 0.96x window median [D1135].
Operating cash flow was 1.32x net income [D450], and the 13.2% free cash flow margin [D447] sits above its 11.9% window median [D1129].
Capital spending rose 41.9% to $2.82 billion [D470][F90], lifting capex to 1.25x D&A [D452]; the filing cites higher capital expenditures in MP&E investing [P3].
Receivables rose 17.6% [D486] and inventories 7.8% [D487] against 4.3% revenue growth [D463]; the filing says these changes partly offset MP&E's operating cash gain [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456], from $24.9 billion in FY2024 [D403], or 38.8% of revenue [D457].
At -38.8% of revenue [D457], net cash sits at the 43rd percentile of seven industrials peers [D1151], against a -35.6% peer median [D1152].
Liquidity is steady, with a current ratio of 1.44x [F180] against a 1.40x window median [D1138] and cash up 44.9% to $10.0 billion [D472][F140].
Buybacks and dividends of $7.9 billion [D458] absorbed 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], down from 102.9% in FY2024 [D406], while diluted shares fell 3.5% [D483].
Operating profit fell 14.7% [D464], the first material decline since FY2020 [D199], on manufacturing costs and tariffs [P9]; medium severity, one year so far.
Net debt has widened two years running [R1]: total debt rose 14.1% to $36.2 billion [D485][D455], and the filing ties Financial Products' financing inflow to borrowing [P2].
FY2025 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded [F40][R3]; the 10-K figure of $8.88 billion [X20] differs by under 0.06%, so growth rates stand.
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 [D410] but rose 4.3% in FY2025 [D463], so the earlier decline is dropped as a flag.
Operating margin: the trend holds while it stays above the 14.3% window median [D1123], from 16.5% [F30]; a fall below 14.3% would reverse it. Filing: FY2026 10-K.
Manufacturing costs: FY2025 absorbed $2.148 billion [P9], and the company guides to higher Power & Energy manufacturing costs in Q1 2026 [P14].
Buybacks plus dividends above the FY2024 level of 102.9% of free cash flow [D406] would mean debt-funded returns continue, widening net debt beyond $26.2 billion [D456].
